title: Transformer Equivalent Circuit, Tests & Efficiency
subtitle: A real transformer has winding resistance, leakage flux, and core losses. The OC and SC tests find parameters experimentally. Maximum efficiency when iron loss = copper loss — this derivation is a guaranteed exam question.

topics.title: OC Test, SC Test & Maximum Efficiency

subtopics.title: OC Test, SC Test & Maximum Efficiency

content.text: Open Circuit Test — LV side excited at rated voltage, HV side open. No secondary current → zero copper loss. Wattmeter reads iron (core) loss only. Gives P_iron and magnetising branch (Ro, Xo).
Short Circuit Test — HV side excited at reduced voltage (3–8% rated), LV side shorted. Tiny flux → negligible iron loss. Wattmeter reads full-load copper loss. Gives P_cu, Req, Zeq, Xeq.
Max efficiency when W_i = W_cu: Iron loss is constant (independent of load). Copper loss = x²×W_cu(FL) where x = fraction of full load. Setting equal: x = √(W_i/W_cu(FL)).

Why kVA not kW? Iron loss depends only on voltage (constant at rated voltage). Copper loss depends only on current. Neither depends on power factor. Total loss = f(V,I) = f(kVA) — independent of cosφ.

Common mistake — OC test → LV side (LV excited, HV open). SC test → HV side (HV excited, LV shorted). Reversing these loses all marks. Also: maximum efficiency ≠ full load — it depends on W_i/W_cu ratio.
